Unmodified copies of NCEI StormEvents_details-ftp_v1.0_d1996..d2025 (creation dates c2026-03 to c2026-05) on GitHub (the files actually parsed)

annual_frequency.note: NCEI Storm Events, Travis County (STATE_FIPS 48, CZ 453), 1996-2025 (30 yrs). Distinct dates with >=2.0 in hail reported anywhere in the county: 14 (0.47/yr) -> ~9 per 20-yr roof life. Low = >=2.5 in: 7 days (0.23/yr, ~5 per 20 yrs). High = >=1.75 in: 32 days (1.07/yr, ~21 per 20 yrs). >=1.0 in: 75 days (2.50/yr, ~50 per 20 yrs; 271 reports). Williamson: >=1 in 81 days (2.70/yr), >=2 in 18 days (0.60/yr), >=1.75 in 33 days. Both counties combined: >=2 in 28 days (0.93/yr). These are COUNTY-WIDE occurrences; any single building is hit far less often (Travis is ~1,000 sq mi and hail swaths are narrow). For per-building expected loss use the NRI ratio instead: hail EAL $23.9M/yr on $189.5B building exposure = ~0.013% of building value per year.

perils.severity_note: Hail is Austin's dominant roof peril. NCEI-recorded property damage from hail 1996-2025: Travis ~$562M, Williamson ~$300M, dominated by a few events: 24 Sep 2023 (4.0 in Williamson / 3.0 in Travis, $300M each county as recorded), 25 Mar 2009 (3.0-3.5 in, $160M Travis), 25 Mar 2005 (2.0 in, $100M Travis). Largest stones 4.0 in (14 May 2008, 24 Sep 2023, 30 May 2024). Decade trend (Travis+Williamson >=2 in hail-days): 6 (1996-2005), 10 (2006-15), 12 (2016-25). NCEI damage figures are rough estimates.

fema_nri.note: Refreshed by scripts/refresh_nri.py so every market uses the same NRI release. annualized_frequency = county-wide events/yr, not hits on one building.

research_fields.note: Ratings are NRI hazard risk ratings (<HAZ>_RISKR). annualized_frequency = events/yr per NRI methodology (hail/strong wind 1986-2021, tornado 1950-2021, winter weather & heat wave 2005-2021, ice storm 1946-2014, riverine flooding 1996-2019). eal_building_usd = expected annual loss to building value for ALL buildings in the county (all occupancies), not commercial roofs specifically. Coastal flooding is 'Not Applicable'. Heat wave is rated 'Relatively High' but NRI assigns only ~$49/yr building EAL: NRI does not model heat/UV roof aging, which is the main climate driver of roof life here. FEMA released NRI v1.20 (Dec 2025); v1.20 values could not be retrieved (hazards.fema.gov blocked) and may differ.

roof_life_years.climate_note: Qualitative only (no sourced number): Austin combines high summer heat/UV (NRI Heat Wave 'Relatively High'), frequent large hail (NRI Hail 'Very High', ~0.5 >=2-in hail-days/yr county-wide) and occasional hard freezes/ice (Feb 2021, Feb 2023). These favor faster membrane/coating aging than cooler climates and make hail, not age, the most common trigger for early replacement. Check data/national.json for cross-market maintained-vs-reactive life evidence.
